about.title: Lindsay Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lindsay is a small city, but its roads carry real traffic pressure, especially where Rt 65 meets Hermosa, Tulare Road, and Mirage Avenue. Public records show 22 injury collisions and 33 injured people in the most recent year, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. as commuters, farmworkers, and weekend traffic overlap. Whether you were hit at an intersection, rear-ended on Tulare Road, or sideswiped near the Rt 65 corridor, the days after a crash matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, damaged vehicle parts, and witness memories fade quickly. LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Lindsay residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, protect your right to compensation, and handle communication with insurers on your behalf, all on a contingency basis, so you owe nothing unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity's vehicle or road was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help identify the correct deadline before you lose the chance to act.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce Your Recovery
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your compensation is reduced by your share of blame. Insurers know this and often push drivers toward statements that shift fault higher than it should be.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash, often before you know the full extent of your injuries. An attorney can speak for you instead, helping preserve evidence and avoid words used later to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Lindsay car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a city or county vehicle or roadway was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth having your situation reviewed early.

items.question: Will fault matter if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partially responsible. Your final recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's important not to accept blame prematurely with an insurer.

items.question: Should I be concerned about giving a statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: Yes — insurers often request recorded statements quickly, sometimes before injuries like those from a Friday-afternoon collision near Rt 65 or Tulare Road fully show up. It's generally safer to let an attorney communicate on your behalf so nothing you say is used to reduce your claim.

items.question: How does LawProactive work if I want help after a crash in Lindsay?
items.answer: LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney in the Lindsay area who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.
